original_question: A null 2-type submanifold is one whose mean curvature vector H satisfies Delta H = lambda H for some nonzero real constant lambda. Study and classify null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 10: "Study and classify null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target open problem in Section 7 and preserves its two emphasized special cases: null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces. It also correctly notices that null 2-type submanifolds are tied to a mean-curvature eigenvalue equation of the form ΔH = λH with λ ≠ 0.
missing_details: In the paper, "null 2-type" is defined spectrally, not directly by the equation ΔH = λH. The ambient immersion x must admit a finite-type decomposition x = c + x1 + x2 with Δx1 = 0 and Δx2 = λx2 for some nonzero real constant λ.
The equation ΔH = λH is presented in Section 7 as a consequence of the null 2-type definition together with the preliminaries, not as the definition itself.

The paper explicitly warns that Euclidean submanifolds satisfying ΔH = λH are not all null 2-type: Section 7 says that biharmonic submanifolds, null 2-type submanifolds, and 1-type submanifolds are the Euclidean submanifolds satisfying that equation, so the draft definition is too broad.
The underlying setting from the preliminaries is an isometric immersion x : M → E^m of a connected Riemannian manifold into real Euclidean space, with Δ the Laplace operator on M.
The mean curvature vector H is linked to the immersion by Beltrami’s formula Δx = -nH, which is part of the nearby context used to derive the mean-curvature equation.
The word "null" refers to the presence of the zero eigenvalue in the spectral decomposition; this finite-type meaning is not stated in the draft.
The paper notes that every null k-type submanifold is non-compact; this is an implicit structural consequence omitted in the draft.

For the Euclidean 4-space case, the nearby context records partial results: null 2-type surfaces in E^4 with constant mean curvature are open portions of helical cylinders, and those with parallel normalized mean curvature vector are open portions of circular cylinders.
The same nearby context says it is still unknown whether every null 2-type surface in E^4 has constant mean curvature; this explains why the E^4 case is singled out in the problem statement.
For the pseudo-Euclidean part, the paper does not fix a single signature; it states the problem broadly for "4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces."
refined_question: Let x : M^n → E^m be a connected isometric immersion of a Riemannian manifold into real Euclidean space, and suppose that x is of null 2-type in the finite-type sense, namely that its spectral decomposition has the form x = c + x1 + x2 with Δx1 = 0 and Δx2 = λx2 for some nonzero real constant λ. Study and classify such null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in E^4 and all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 7 rather than the paper’s earlier conjectures on finite-type surfaces in E^3. The exact official target is Problem 10 in Section 7. To make the question paper-faithful, the main correction is definitional: Section 2.1 defines null 2-type through the spectral decomposition of the immersion, while Section 7 only derives the consequence ΔH = λH from that definition and the preliminaries. Section 7 also states that Euclidean submanifolds satisfying the mean-curvature eigenvalue equation are not automatically null 2-type, because 1-type submanifolds also fall under that equation; hence the draft’s opening sentence is too broad. The refined version therefore keeps the exact scope of Problem 10 while replacing the draft’s PDE-based definition by the paper’s actual spectral one and preserving the two special classification targets emphasized by the paper.
